title: Group/lane label text isn't legible across gradient backgrounds (single global luminance sample)
description:
Bug: lane/group header text (e.g. "UNSORTED", "EMBERSTONE" — .lane-title, .lane-tab-count, .lane-delete-btn, .lane-collapse-btn) goes low-contrast against parts of the new default background (img/landscape.jpg), which has a strong luminance gradient from dark teal top-left to light peach bottom-right. See screenshot in chat 99df29a9 (image-3.png): "UNSORTED" is barely readable against the teal corner while "EMBERSTONE" lower on the page reads fine.

Root cause: components/SettingsPanel.js `applyOnBackground(lum)` sets one global --on-bg / --on-bg-muted / --on-bg-shadow pair from a single averaged luminance value for the whole wallpaper (see lumSum averaging around line ~1385, and lastBgLum/applyOnBackground around line 1565-1642). That's a fine model for a background with roughly uniform luminance, but breaks down for a gradient/photo where luminance varies a lot across the viewport — one global light-or-dark text choice can't be correct everywhere.

Fix needed: make on-background text contrast-aware per label position rather than globally. Some directions to evaluate (pick what's cleanest, don't need to do all):
1. Sample local luminance under/near each .lane-title's actual rendered rect (e.g. via a small offscreen canvas draw of the background image cropped to that element's approximate position) instead of one whole-image average, and set the on-bg vars per-lane (or per-label) rather than on :root.
2. If per-element sampling is too heavy, at minimum strengthen the always-on text-shadow/scrim (--on-bg-shadow) so it guarantees contrast regardless of local luminance — e.g. a bigger blur/spread outline rather than a soft 1px shadow, so light-on-dark or dark-on-light both stay legible even when the global pick is "wrong" for that spot.
3. Consider whether a translucent scrim/backdrop strip behind lane headers (similar to --card-bg) is simpler and more robust than trying to solve pure luminance-derived text color for photos with high local variance.

Whatever approach you land on, verify specifically against img/landscape.jpg in both light and dark theme, and check it doesn't regress the existing behavior on more uniform backgrounds (solids, gradients with low variance, other photos, "none").

Mind the existing comment/intent at meridian.css ~505-515 ("Lane headers sit on the wallpaper, not a surface — use luminance-derived on-background text so they stay legible against any background.") — the intent is right, the single global sample is the bug.
label: Bug

activity.content:
Implemented a local contrast surface for every lane header.

- Scoped the on-background text variables to each .lane-header and placed them over a 94%-opaque, blurred theme surface, eliminating dependence on one wallpaper-wide luminance sample.
- Strengthened the muted token with a primary/secondary mix and removed the tab-count opacity that reduced effective contrast.
- Mirrored runtime changes into meridian-extension and updated the luminance-solver comments to document the local override.
- Added regression coverage proving the scoped scrim exists and that muted labels retain at least 4.5:1 contrast over worst-case black and white wallpaper pixels in light and dark themes.

Verification: node --test tests/*.test.mjs passed all 158 tests; git diff --check passed; packaged CSS and SettingsPanel sources match. Headed Chromium screenshots using img/landscape.jpg confirmed legible upper and lower lane headers in explicit light and dark themes.
